sample_unit: annotated text chunks from clinical notes

links.outcome: Classifier F1 when fine-tuned on in-domain versus other-specialty data
links.effect: GatorTron fine-tuned on OB-GYN reached F1 0.96 in-domain; tested on MIMIC-IV, F1 fell below 0.70 (44% drop). Training on MIMIC-IV then testing on OB-GYN gave F1 0.71 (11% drop) with reduced precision.
links.quote: Our findings demonstrate that fine-tuning outperforms prompting for emotional valence classification and that models must be adapted to specific medical specialties to achieve clinically appropriate performance.

links.outcome: Performance drop when model applied to a different specialty and health system
links.effect: External validation on MIMIC-IV showed F1 below 0.70, a 44% drop from the OB-GYN test set.
links.quote: External validation on MIMIC-IV revealed limited cross-domain generalizability (F1 < 0.70, 44% drop).

unlisted_practices: Supervised fine-tuning with lexically primed inputs outperforms zero-shot and in-context prompting for clinical-note bias detection
Detecting stigmatizing language in clinical documentation

screen.reason: Evaluates NLP/LLM classification strategies (prompting vs fine-tuning) on an annotated dataset of clinical notes to detect biased/stigmatizing language, with no organizational deployment safeguard tested.
